key_insight: Flexible modular robots combine movement and object manipulation in the same unit. By physically connecting, they form task-adaptive structures that cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Robots with fixed bodies can struggle when different tasks require different physical capabilities. This work addresses that limitation through flexible modules that cooperate and change their collective form.
method: Use flexible tensegrity continuum robot modules that support both locomotion and manipulation.
Physically connect modules into cooperative structures adapted to the task.
Apply these configurations to object transport, gap crossing and challenging terrain.
impact: The work highlights how adaptable robot bodies can complement control and coordination. For AI and robotics practitioners, it motivates systems that consider physical configuration alongside movement and task planning.
visual_elements: Labeled illustration of a flexible robot module showing locomotion and manipulation.
Sequence showing separate modules connecting into a task-adaptive structure.
Three task panels: carrying an object, crossing a gap and traversing uneven terrain.
Concept diagram linking task requirements to robot configuration and cooperative action.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
